inputs.original_text: An Indiana judge blocked a law restricting abortion after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued it burdened people’s ability to follow their sincerely held religious beliefs. That’s a crucial check on state power: no government should impose one religious or political worldview by restricting people’s bodily autonomy and access to care. These restrictions fall hardest on people with the fewest resources and choices. LifeNews.com’s “killing babies” language is inflammatory framing, not a serious engagement with religious freedom or the real consequences of denying care.
inputs.modified_text: An Indiana judge has blocked a law restricting abortion after the ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice framed the restriction as a burden on religious belief. That turns religious liberty into a weapon against the state’s responsibility to protect unborn life. No one’s freedom is unlimited, and calling abortion access “care” doesn’t erase the moral stakes or the interests of the most vulnerable. The real question is whether the law may uphold a society’s duty to defend life—not whether bodily autonomy should always trump it.
